item.text: {"text":"Recent evidence separates history usefulness from complex sequence reasoning. A [RecSys 2026 study](https://research.atspotify.com/2026/10/do-sequential-recommendation-benchmarks-require-higher-order-sequence-modelling) found history-aware pairwise transition models outperforming SASRec/eSASRec reproductions on four of five benchmarks; older interactions helped even without joint contextualization. These results concern different Amazon categories and evaluation settings, so they motivate controls rather than predict RecHarness gains. [BSARec (2024)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/28747) identifies attention oversmoothing and introduces frequency-based modeling; [LISRec (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.22130) selects semantically connected history subsets. Together, these suggest distinguishing broad semantic associations, recent-item effects, and contextual interactions rather than treating all history sensitivity as useful personalization.\n\nProposed diagnostic synthesis: compare matched early/recent replacements, recent-window permutations, and older-prefix changes with the last item fixed. Match replacement popularity and title/description similarity using training data; preserve sequence length, padding positions, causal prefixes, and candidate sets. Measure paired candidate-margin changes, rank shifts, top-10 overlap, and validation HR@10. Compare full predictions against last-item-only, order-invariant history, pairwise-transition, and residual/backbone ablations; distinguish inference-time component removal from retrained ablations. Validate specificity with synthetic popularity-only, last-item-only, and order-invariant scorers, plus identity interventions. These controls are proposed methodology, not an established standardized suite. History-edit explanations, such as [Demystifying Sequential Recommendations (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.03606), establish model response to hypothetical inputs—not causal user preferences. Use findings to test gated recent/history branches, explicit transition components, or targeted contrastive training; retain changes only when macro validation HR@10 improves."}
